reasons: Some parameter records are preserved for provenance but are not consumed by the reference runtime: log_kow

supported_substance_classes: neutral or weakly sorbing organic chemicals under screening-level multimedia assumptions
release scenarios that can be approximated as regional mass loading into air, water, soil, or sediment compartments
deterministic assessor-review and benchmark workflows that require transparent concentration-only outputs
unsupported_substance_classes: metals and metal species requiring speciation-aware fate treatment
nanomaterials or particulate systems requiring size-resolved transport behavior
strongly ionizing chemistries where screening partition and persistence assumptions are likely unstable
assessments dominated by transformation products, food-chain transfer, or explicit intermedia transfer kinetics
required_inputs: media-specific capacity defaults or governed overrides
media-specific half-life defaults or governed overrides
core_assumptions: The runtime emits regional concentration surfaces rather than dose, exposure, or risk values.
Each release medium is represented as a single screening compartment with governed capacity defaults.
Finite-duration first-order decay is applied over the declared release duration and any post-release elapsed time.
Steady-state mode reports the end-of-duration screening concentration rather than an infinite-time equilibrium.
Only treatment assumptions explicitly marked as pre_release_global are numerically applied before release; all other treatment assumptions remain provenance-only.
Reference mass balance does not add explicit advective clearance or intermedia transfer terms.
review_notes: Use for concentration-only screening support, benchmark demonstrations, and downstream suite handoff preparation.
Review unsupported runtime parameters before treating outputs as more than screening indicators.
Escalate to richer model families when multiple complex media interactions dominate the decision context.
applicability_profile.applicability_note: Reference mass balance is appropriate for transparent deterministic screening workflows inside the declared Fate MCP boundary.
